behavioral_notes.observation: Requests flow across maintenance.stage kanban columns (demo: New Request -> In Progress -> Repaired -> Scrap; the last two have done=True). maintenance_type selects 'corrective' (default) vs 'preventive'. Moving to any done stage sets close_date=today and triggers activity_feedback/activity_update; moving back clears close_date. write() also resets kanban_state to 'normal' on stage change. Stage semantics live in Python, not metadata.

Preventive recurrence is NOT a cron. In write(), when a recurring preventive request enters a done stage, the record copy()s itself with schedule_date advanced by repeat_interval x repeat_unit (day/week/month/year) and reset to the first stage, honoring repeat_type forever/until repeat_until. _compute_recurring_maintenance forces recurring_maintenance=False unless maintenance_type=='preventive'. (Note: stale i18n still references a removed next_action_date field / maintenance_requests_cron server action; neither exists in the current models/maintenance.py.)

equipment_id (ondelete='restrict') links a request to its asset; category_id is related/stored from equipment_id.category_id, and _compute_user_id assigns the technician from equipment.technician_user_id (fallback category.technician_user_id). create/write call _add_followers (message_subscribe owner+technician) and activity_schedule/reschedule a 'maintenance.mail_act_maintenance_request' activity on schedule_date. These cross-model effects are invisible to metadata.

Abstract mixin (inherited by maintenance.equipment) computes reliability KPIs in _compute_maintenance_request from done corrective requests: mttr = avg(close_date - request_date); mtbf = (latest_failure_date - effective_date)/count; estimated_next_failure = latest_failure_date + mtbf days; expected_mtbf is a manual target. Formulas are Python-only.

7 JS files, 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components; 1 registry registration 'views:calendar_with_recurrence' (a custom calendar view extension under static/src/views/calendar_with_recurrence rendering recurring preventive requests); asset bundles ['web.assets_backend', 'web.assets_tests']. No portal/website frontend.

classification.rationale: Maintenance is a firm-infrastructure support activity (Stabell & Fjeldstad: a value-shop-shaped diagnostic/repair routine wrapped around the asset base, but classified support because it sustains the firm's productive assets rather than transforming a customer order). It does not buy, make, or sell anything tradeable; it keeps equipment serviceable so the primary value chain (mrp/stock) can run. APQC PCF 10.0 'Acquire, Construct, and Manage Assets' owns asset maintenance: 10.5 (Maintain productive assets) covers the corrective request lifecycle and 10.5.x preventive maintenance scheduling matches the recurring preventive cron-like copy mechanism. (8.x 'Manage Information Technology' was rejected: the assets here are physical equipment, not IT services.) MTBF/MTTR KPIs and the equipment register are textbook asset-management instrumentation.

standard_capabilities: equipment / asset register with categories, serial, warranty, cost, scrap date
corrective & preventive maintenance request kanban (configurable stages)
maintenance teams, email-alias request intake, technician auto-assignment
MTBF/MTTR reliability KPIs + team dashboard + pivot/graph reporting
typical_fits: asset-tracked corrective + preventive maintenance with stage pipeline
common_gaps: spare-parts / inventory consumption on a work order (needs maintenance_worksheet or stock integration)
meter / usage-based preventive triggers (only calendar-interval recurrence is built in)
labor costing / billing of maintenance work (no native cost capture beyond duration)
SLA / response-time enforcement beyond the activity deadline
